title: Identifying mechanosensitive nuclear proteins in mammalian cells
author: Tseng, Sun, et al.

steps.title: Seed and treat cells for biotinylation
steps.instruction: Seed 6.5 × 10⁶ HEK293‑tet‑RhoA‑TurboID cells in a 100 mm dish and incubate 24 h to reach ~90 % confluency. Add 1 µg ml⁻¹ tetracycline (or 1 µl 70 % ethanol as vehicle control) and incubate 2 h at 37 °C. Then add biotin to a final concentration of 500 µM and incubate 20 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cells and prepare streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium and wash cells five times with ice‑cold PBS. Lyse cells in ice‑cold RIPA buffer using a standard protocol. Aliquot 100 µl streptavidin‑agarose beads, keep on ice, and wash three times with ice‑cold RIPA buffer by centrifugation at 1 800 × g for 2 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Bind lysate to beads and incubate
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant from the bead wash and add the cell lysate (containing ≈3000 µg total protein) to the beads. Incubate overnight on a constant roller at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash beads with sequential buffers
steps.instruction: Transfer the bead‑lysate mixture to a Wizard R‑Mini‑column and wash the beads sequentially with: 10 ml 2 % SDS, 10 ml RIPA buffer, 10 ml 0.5 M NaCl, 10 ml 2 M urea/50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, and finally 10 ml 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.

steps.title: Resuspend beads for downstream processing
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed beads in 120 µl 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate and transfer to a fresh Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Elute proteins for western blot
steps.instruction: Mix 20 µl of the bead suspension with 20 µl 2× Laemmli buffer, then boil 5 min at 98 °C to elute biotinylated proteins. Boiled samples in Laemmli buffer may be frozen at –20 °C for up to 3 months before blotting.

steps.title: Perform western blot analysis
steps.instruction: Detect biotinylated proteins using Alexa Fluor 680 Streptavidin Conjugate. Probe for YAP in the nuclear fraction, and also blot nucleolin (nuclear marker) and β‑tubulin (cytosolic marker) to confirm streptavidin‑pulldown selectivity.

steps.title: On‑bead reduction and alkylation
steps.instruction: Wash the remaining bead slurry (~100 µl) with 1 ml 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, centrifuge 1 800 × g for 3 min at room temperature, and discard supernatant. Incubate beads in 200 µl 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 10 mM TCEP for 15 min at 37 °C with shaking. Add 4 µl 0.5 M iodoacetamide, incubate 15 min in the dark at 37 °C with shaking.

steps.title: Overnight tryptic digestion on beads
steps.instruction: Add 1 µg sequencing‑grade trypsin to the beads and digest overnight at 37 °C with shaking. The next day, centrifuge 1 800 × g for 1 min at room temperature and transfer the supernatant (peptide fragments) to a clean tube.

steps.title: Acidify peptide eluate and store
steps.instruction: Add 14 µl 10 % TFA to the peptide solution to lower pH to ~3 (verify with pH indicator strips). Acidified peptides may be stored at –80 °C for up to 6 months; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare C18 stage tip for desalting
steps.instruction: Using clean scissors, cut off approximately one‑quarter from the top and bottom of a 1 ml blue tip; this modified tip will attach to an uncut 1 ml tip to form a stable C18 stage tip. Wash the tip with 100 µl 0.1 % TFA/50 % acetonitrile (ACN) to fully wet the resin.

steps.title: Load, wash, and elute peptides
steps.instruction: Transfer the acidified peptide solution into the prepared stage tip, flick gently to remove bubbles, and slowly pipette the sample through the tip. Collect the flow‑through in the original tube and repeat once for improved binding. Wash the tip three times with 100 µl 0.1 % TFA. Elute peptides by slowly passing 100 µl 0.1 % TFA/50 % ACN into a fresh 2 ml Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Dry and reconstitute peptides for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Dry the eluate in a vacuum concentrator for 90 min at 45 °C. Add 10–40 µl 0.5 % formic acid, incubate 10 min at 21 °C with shaking, then transfer the peptide solution to an autosampler vial compatible with the LC‑MS/MS system. Peptide solutions may be stored at –80 °C for up to 6 months. (C18 spin columns can be used as an alternative to stage tips.)

steps.title: Process raw MS data with MaxQuant
steps.instruction: Run MaxQuant (v1.6.2.6 or newer) against the latest human UniProt database (UP000005640). Set digestion to Trypsin/P with up to 2 missed cleavages; variable modifications: methionine oxidation, N‑terminal acetylation; fixed modification: carbamidomethyl‑Cys. Enable ‘match between runs’ (match window 0.7 min, alignment window 20 min). Activate label‑free quantification (LFQ) with minimum ratio count 2, minimum neighbors 3, average neighbors 6. Set first‑search tolerance 20 ppm, main‑search tolerance 4.5 ppm for FTMS and 0.5 Da for ITMS. Use protein and peptide FDR 0.01.

steps.title: Statistical analysis in Perseus
steps.instruction: Export the MaxQuant proteinGroups.txt file and open in Perseus (v1.5.6.0 or newer). Load LFQ intensities to the ‘Main’ category and protein/gene names to the ‘Text’ category. Group replicates using the Categorical Annotation Rows function. Log2‑transform LFQ intensities, then remove proteins quantified in fewer than three replicates of any group. Generate a histogram to verify normal distribution. Compute Pearson correlations (Column correlation) and visualise with multi‑scatter plots. Impute missing values using a down‑shifted normal distribution (default settings, adjust if needed). Perform PCA to visualise group separation. Conduct a two‑sample t‑test with permutation‑based FDR 0.05; adjust the S₀ parameter (typically 0.1–2) as desired. Visualise significant changes with a volcano plot (same parameters).
